sections.overview: This elusive rattlesnake is known from western Mexico, especially the Sierra de Manantlán region of Jalisco.
sections.identification: It has a slender, unusually long tail and a gray ground colour marked with dark dorsal blotches.
sections.habitat: Available records place it in rocky grassland near the transition between tropical deciduous and pine-oak forests.
sections.diet: The Mexican species account lists lizards, arthropods and other reptiles among its reported prey.
sections.behavior: It may be active at dusk or night and has been observed thermoregulating beside grasses or on low shrubs.
sections.reproduction: Reliable species-specific breeding information is scarce in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: It belongs to the rare long-tailed rattlesnake group, alongside Crotalus stejnegeri and Crotalus ericsmithi.
sections.conservation: Mexico lists it as threatened; rediscovery reports and few locality records underline the need for further surveys.

sources.title: Rediscovery of the rare Autlán long-tailed rattlesnake
